title: 140 ETH lost to address poisoning (Ethereum, 14 Aug 2025)
summary: The victim sent 140 ETH to a lookalike of an address it had paid before, after copying it from a contaminated transfer history (as reported by Scam Sniffer).

public_sources.title: Address poisoning: victim / wrong address / correct address
public_sources.used_for: Victim, lookalike and correct addresses; harmful transaction link. Retrieved by a research subagent on 2026-10-27; values cross-checked on-chain, page not re-read by hand.

public_sources.title: Crypto address poisoning scammers netted $1.6M this week
public_sources.used_for: Amount and mechanism (no addresses). Retrieved by a research subagent on 2026-10-27; values cross-checked on-chain, page not re-read by hand.

harm.description: The victim signed a native transfer of 140 ETH to the lookalike (token field 0x0 = native ETH).

evaluation.rationale: The 21,600 blocks (about 3 days) before and including the harmful block: the same round default as the WBTC case, fixed before any activity in the window was examined.

onchain_verification: Verified on 2026-10-28 via eth.drpc.org: tx 0x4d27c67a...e1d6 in block 23141530, from the victim to 0xC61756E0Ea2933Ad8ec8be11cb444c4215c23B86, value 140 ETH, status success, no Transfer logs.
Verified: eth_getCode(victim) empty at block 23141530 (plain EOA); nonce 3 at block 23119930 and 5 after block 23141530.
ground_truth_limitations: Attribution as poisoning rests on one security firm's public post plus the prefix/suffix match; no confirmed attribution.
The planting step was not independently located before recording; the replay uses only what the fixture contains.
